findings.summary: The complete explicit six-coloring and exhaustive exact checker support that {1,…,536} has no monochromatic solution to x+y=z, and hence support S(6)≥536 with high confidence.

The certificate is fully present and independently replayable, but the transaction contains only expected output rather than an actual execution transcript or hosted attestation; the judgment therefore does not claim independent performance of all 71,824 comparisons.

The Python checker soundly validates the compact and expanded encodings, exact coverage and color ranges, representation agreement, and every relevant pair x≤y with x+y≤536 using exact deterministic integer arithmetic.

The checker is specialized to n=536, six colors, and symmetry modulus 537 rather than being a general Schur-instance verifier; its canonicalization applies to labeled colorings and does not quotient by color-label permutations.

The transaction provides neither a coloring of 537 nor an impossibility certificate or new upper bound, so it does not improve either endpoint or determine S(6); the supported interval remains 536≤S(6)≤1836.
